title: Oak Avenue Retrofit integration play notes
content:
Context:
- Customer: Oak Avenue Pharmacies (regional retail chain, ~120 locations).
- Use case: In-store pharmacist assistant to surface drug interactions and guideline snippets from internal SOPs plus public sources. Must run in VPC; cannot send PHI to hosted model.
- Engagement stage: technical kickoff + pilot scope; exploring Redwood Private (VPC) deployment with option to move to Dedicated later.

Call notes (2025-11-12, 14:00 PST) — participants: Maya (Rwd), Diego (Rwd), Priya (Rwd SE), Aaron White (Oak Eng), Saira Khan (Oak Product), DevOps: Ben Cho
- Intro: Oak wants low-latency Q&A (aim <250ms p50 for short prompts) for local kiosk and tablet clients. 2K qps burst expected during shift changes across fleet.
- Data: SOP docs + internal KB ≈ 22GB plaintext, plus nightly feed of 500MB structured update. All must remain inside their VPC.
- Compliance: PHI may appear in queries. Oak requires strict KMS integration (BYOK) and audit logs at token-level for a 30-day retention window.
- Model selection: Oak prefers an open LLM (Llama2-70B or MPT-30B style) but will accept a smaller tuned base if latency/cost trade-offs reasonable. They asked about quantized CPU fallback for on-prem branch offices.
- Availability: want 99.9% overall SLA but can tolerate short degrade to lower-capacity model for <10m/day if primary pool unavailable.
- Connectivity: initial plan is VPC peering to Redwood control plane with encrypted egress; ops team will wire up a transit gateway.

Key technical requirements (synthesized):
1) Private deployment: control plane in Redwood, inference plane inside Oak VPC (customer-managed subnets), support for HSM/KMS with BYOK.
2) Latency SLOs: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 700ms for typical 32-token continuations. Need baseline perf numbers per model variant and concrete perf tuning steps (batching, kv-cache warmup).
3) Throughput: baseline steady 200 qps, bursts to 2K qps for ~5–10 minutes, autoscale to handle bursts without cold-starting new nodes beyond 30s.
4) Data residency: logs, prompts, and KV cache must remain in customer VPC; only aggregated metrics are shared with Redwood telemetry.
5) Security: mTLS with cert rotation; token-level audit logs; SOC2/ISO references in contract.
6) Cost control: suggest Redwood Optimize recommendations — quantization + small cache window for low-cost mode.
7) Fallback behavior: automated fallback to smaller model or cached answer if primary model overloaded; configurable policy per route.

Gotchas / risks flagged on call:
- Network egress patterns: Oak's firewall team is strict — initial VPC peering test blocked control-plane-to-agent heartbeat. Need pre-flight network checklist and sample ACLs before deployment.
- Latency mismatch: their 250ms p50 target is aggressive for 70B models on cold cache unless we use local GPU pool with pinned capacity; estimate p50 ~450ms on soft shared nodes. Need to produce bench numbers for our supported model builds.
- Audit log volume: token-level logging for 2K qps will create heavy storage + ingestion costs (approx estimate: 200K tokens/sec at peak => 17GB/hr raw). Oak is sensitive to cost and retention; propose sampled token logs + full audit for flagged sessions.
- BYOK/HSM: their procurement timeline for HSM certification is slow — may be a blocker for pilot. Suggest a short-term mitigant: customer-managed KMS without HSM for pilot, with contractual constraints.
- Model drift/regression: Oak will need prompt-set based quality monitoring tied to rollout policies. We should offer an eval harness mapped to their SOP-critical questions.

Immediate action items (owners + rough due dates):
- Maya: Deliver model perf matrix (p50/p95/throughput) for 3 candidate configs (mpt-30b-8bit, rw-13b-quant, 70b-8bit-dist) — due 2025-11-18 (Linear REDW-1287).
- Diego: Draft VPC preflight checklist + example Security Group/route table snippets to share with Oak infra — due 2025-11-14.
- Priya: Prepare brief on audit log sampling schemes, cost estimate for 30-day full token retention vs sampling — due 2025-11-17.
- Aaron (Oak): Confirm procurement timeline for BYOK/HSM or approval for temporary KMS-only pilot — target 2025-11-21.
- Ben (Oak): Arrange a test VPC peering window next week (preferred: 11/17 10:00–11:00 PST) and provide contact for infra on-call.

Open questions to resolve (high priority):
- Acceptance criteria for pilot success (SLO thresholds, cost per inference target, sample QA queries). Need a short joint doc.
- Will Oak allow any telemetry (aggregated traces) during pilot or is zero telemetry mandatory? Clarify minimal telemetry set to keep ops viable.
- Fallback policy: prefer auto-fallback or explicit canary switch? We should propose a canned policy with opt-in auto-fallback + alerts.

Notes for internal follow-up:
- For perf matrix, include tokenization and end-to-end (client -> model -> client) numbers, not just raw model inference. Instrument approximate network RTT assumptions (intra-VPC, ~5–12ms).
- Check if Redwood Optimize rules can recommend a dynamic quantization schedule for daytime (low-latency) vs night (cost-saver). Could be a selling point.
- Consider building a small eval-suite of 40 SOP questions (golden set) to run daily against new rollouts — Priya to scope.

Meeting artifacts to attach to proposal:
- VPC checklist (Diego)
- Perf matrix (Maya)
- Audit log options (Priya)
- Pilot success criteria draft (joint doc)

Next scheduled sync: 2025-11-19 09:00 PST (tentative) — goal: align on pilot acceptance criteria and confirm peering test.

Quick wins to push before next sync:
- Send a 1-pager pilot plan (2 slides + checklist) summarizing what we will deliver in the 6-week pilot.
- Run a quick local perf microbenchmark for mpt-30b-8bit on a pinned GPU node and share numbers (Maya).

Random notes / shorthand that matter:
- p50 250ms ask seems driven by kiosk UX; product prefers <200ms if possible but can settle at 250ms.
- Token-level audit -> consider gzip+delta compression for storage savings.
- If BYOK delayed, warn legal: partial BYOK may change contract language for data processing.

End of notes.

(Mostly raw; move to proposal doc once we collect perf numbers and Oak confirms BYOK decision.)
